old_title: Crystal Palace v Manchester City: Premier League - live
new_title: Crystal Palace 1-4 Manchester City: Premier League - as it happened
old_text:
A worrying stat for Palace: Mateta and Sarr, two absentees tonight, scored 21 Premier League goals between them last season. Tonight's starting XI for Palace against scored ... 10 between them last season.
City might be Pep-less - which still feels weird - but they do still look formidable. Nobody won possession more times than Elliot Anderson last season (306 times). Nobody provided more assists per 90 minutes than Rayan Cherki. Both players start tonight.
Palace line-up in that familiar 3-4-2-1 formation, although that front three is fluid. For all Palace's problems at centre-back, Tomiyasu, Richards and Canvot (the latter really impressed me last season) are more than dependable and Axel Disasi is on the bench.
No Ismaïla Sarr in the squad, with the Senegalese linked with Liverpool. What a disappointment that he is not playing. No Jean-Philippe Mateta, he is apparently injured, although it is well known he is also anchoring for a move away. Interesting that Daniel Muñoz, reportedly subject of a £22m bid from Nottingham Forest this week, is on the bench. New £21m signing from Union Saint-Gilloise, Anan Khalaili, starts at right-wing back. At least Adam Wharton is there, Palace fans!
As mentioned, Marc Guéhi continues in defensive midfield for City, alongside Elliot Anderson. Rayan Cherki starts after his impressive cameo off the bench against Bournemouth. Ayyoub Bouaddi is on the bench but there is no Jack Grealish, which surely means that he is off: Everton and Sunderland are potential destinations.
Enzo Maresca, Manchester City manager, has been speaking to Sky about his continued use of Marc Guéhi in midfield.
After the Arsenal game [in the Community Shield], we struggled a bit in the middle of the field. This is a league where you need strong midfielders. Marc can do this job. On the ball, he is strong, off the ball he is defensively strong, he gives balance to the team. It's good to be versatile. Bouaddi is an unbelievable player but he is 18, he is young, from France, he needs time.
Ideally we will have two players for every position. Hopefully we can get one more in, or two in. Also maybe one or two out.
That Palace's Holmesdale Fanatics fan group are "stopping all organised activity" at Selhurst Park is particularly sad.
Here are some of the finest tifos by the Holmesdale Fanatics over the years.
Below is a tifo in memory of Maxi Jazz in May 2023, unveiled alongside Faithless lyrics from God Is a DJ that read "This is our church. This is where we heal our hurts". Maxi died in December 2022. He was a West Norwood resident, a Palace supporter and in September 2012 he became an associate director of the club.
Below: a tifo before the Conference League final against Rayo Vallecano in May.
Below: a tifo showing Joel Ward lifting the FA Cup in August 2025, a few months after the 1-0 win over Manchester City at Wembley.
Below: a 2022 tifo depicting the Crystal Palace, built for the Great Exhibition in 1851.
Below: a tifo display celebrating 100 years of Selhurst Park, in September 2024.
Below: a tifo, at the 2025 FA Cup final, depicts three Palace supporters - father Mark Wealleans and sons Nathan and Dominic - who were once seen at Old Trafford in 2011 celebrating Darren Ambrose's sensational strike against Manchester United. After Mark died of cancer in 2017, the image became a symbol of lost loved ones for Palace fans. Nathan and Dominic were in the crowd at Wembley in 2025 and were unaware that the tifo was planned until they saw the image of themselves and their late father with their own eyes.
"I had no idea it was going to be us," Nathan later admitted. "I thought it was going to be something to do with a player retiring this season. Then out of nowhere someone told us and then we broke down in tears as soon as we saw. It was special, it shows there's still a real love for not just my dad, but all the loved ones who love Palace and didn't get to see it. All of them now know we're on the next step."
On Thursday, the Holmesdale Fanatics released the following statement, explaining their reasons for ceasing operations:
Increasingly driven out by the sky high ticket prices, needless restrictions that are designed to strip away the dignity of supporters and relentless harassment and legal action, many young people are choosing to opt out of a game which seems determined to push them away.
We have repeatedly warned the club that likeminded fans cannot congregate at Palace in the numbers required to sustain a growing active supporter culture. The conditions are simply not there. There needs to be a drastic shift at Palace towards younger fans and a move away from a culture in which people attend the ground expecting to be entertained, towards a culture of supporters turning up to play an active role in influencing the result.
The story away from home is even more dire. In domestic away fixtures, supporters are banned from bringing materials into stadiums, coaches are regularly stopped, and fans are arrested. Away ends across the country are increasingly dominated by older fans, with the next generation failing to come through in significant numbers.
Given these conditions, we have immense pride in all the group has achieved over the past 20 years. From being at the heart of the protests that rescued the club in 2010, to securing the away ticket price cap that has saved working class people millions and supporting the club through a record breaking period, the Holmesdale Fanatics has helped write a chapter in the club's history that many did not believe was possible.
But now is the time for us to recognise we have taken the Holmesdale Fanatics as far as it can go in the current climate. We are therefore choosing to stop all organised activity as the Holmesdale Fanatics inside the stadium. We do not take this decision lightly.
In recent years, Palace's success has been built on their cohesion. Despite the significant departures in Michael Olise, Marc Guéhi and Eberechi Eze, Palace have won the FA Cup and a European trophy and secured strong mid-table finishes despite significant departures in Michael Olise, Marc Guéhi and Eberechi Eze. Recruitment has been excellent and the fans have never wavered, always passionately supporting their team, especially at home.
Pierre Sage, only a few weeks into the new job, is already fighting fires. Jean-Philippe Mateta is injured but wants out, as does Daniel Munoz - Nottingham Forest, now managed by Oliver Glasner, reportedly tabled a £22m bid this week for the Colombian. There is a Maxence Lacroix-shaped hole at the back and a deal for his replacement, Joel Ordonez, could be called off after complications with the Club Brugge defender's medical. Meanwhile, Holmesdale Fanatics, Palace's ultras group, has announced that it is disbanding. In short, it's chaos in SE25, which will be music to City's ears.
new_text:
Right, that's me done. Thanks for reading and for your emails. Congrats to City. Palace have a lot of work/business to do before the deadline day on Tuesday. Cheers!
We're watching that first Cherki goal back on the replays now, and it's so special. The thing about Cherki is that he is two-footed and - this seems like a basic point to make perhaps - but each touch of the ball is so measured.
Cherki knows when to take a heavier touch out of his feet (or maybe to move past a defender) and when to nimbly dance with those delicate touches. Sometimes it looks like he's running into a cul-de-sac, only to somehow wriggle out of it. An outrageous talent.
Elliot Anderson, City midfielder, is next to speak:
I enjoyed it today, I've had a few more sessions. I feel like I'm getting better. I'm always nervous when I go on the pitch but my first start at the Etihad was pretty special. It's a big price tag, which everyone is going on about, but I'm just trying to do my best. Just trying to learn on the job. An era has come to an end at City and there's a new one now.
Watching Cherki and Foden, I'm so happy to be playing with them rather than against them. The talent is scary.
Erling Haaland, City goalscorer, speaks to Sky Sports:
We'll be back, we just need a few games. We played well. It's a new manager but we've been playing together. We have to trust the system and trust Enzo.
We have so many good players so we have to fit everyone in. Phil [Foden] has to work hard like everyone else. This was a good start. Elliot [Anderson] was also incredible.
City's Rayan Cherki, player of the match, also speaks:
My performance was so-so, because in first half we didn't find the space and I played so shit. I looked to Enzo and I knew I needed to change it for the second half.
90+4 min: City have enjoyed 78% possession in this second half. Palace have not laid a glove on the visitors since Cherki scored City's third just before the hour.
90 min: Five minutes added on. Palace's next two matches are, mercifully, Fulham and Ipswich, although of course there is no guarantee of points from those two matches.
87 min: After a poor Community Shield and a fortunate win over Bournemouth, it's difficult to know if City have motored into gear here? Or if Palace are just not very good? Maybe Oliver Glasner knew something we didn't.
GOAL! Crystal Palace 1-4 Manchester City (Haaland 85)
He's barely had a kick all game, but Haaland has two goals. Foden, now playing in the No 10 role with McAidoo wide right, has had a mixed match but really excels here, carrying the ball into the Palace area and perfectly feeding Haaland. The weight of pass onto the striker's left foot is **chefs kiss* and although it is an acute angle, Haaland arrows his shot into the roof of the net to render Henderson helpless. FINISH.
83 min: McAidoo almost makes an instant impact. The City academy graduate, who has absolutely tore things up at youth level, nearly scores a sensational solo goal in his first two minutes of Premier League football. McAidoo carries the ball a full 40 yards from the half-way line, cuts inside Disasi, and fires juuuuuuuust wide. So close.
77 min: Yes, this is Manchester City, but one worries for Palace this season, particularly if they lose Mateta, Sarr and Munoz before the window shuts.
Palace swap Khalaili and Tomiyasu for Axel Disasi and Mingueza. Khalaili actually took too long getting off the pitch - 24 seconds - so Palace are penalised and Mingueza is prevented from coming on. That's new in the rules, players have to get a move on. Palace are playing with 10 men for a minute, as Mingueza waits for the ball to go dead. Boos around the stadium but rules are rules.
71 min: Palace are really missing Sarr (or a ball-carrying wide man ... Eze, Olise, Zaha) this evening. Semenyo has been that direct threat for City, and his ability to scare teams in behind has also opened the spaces in front of Palace's defence, for Cherki etc.
66 min: Chance for Palace! Guehi mis-controls the ball and Pino canters into open space. Palace are queuing up at the back post - Nketiah and Guessand free - but Pino overcooks the cross. Again.
63 min: Palace with their first change: Evann Guessand for Jorgen Strand Larsen. Not a good night for the Palace striker, who has generally struggled since his big-money move from Wolves.
61 min: That is a devastating blow for the home side. The crowd really reacted to that Palace goal but the air has completely gone out of the stadium now. City can play keep ball, unless Palace can muster another response.
GOAL! Crystal Palace 1-3 Manchester City (Cherki 59)
City instantly regain their two-goal lead! Cherki pops up in a pocket of space, and lets fly from the edge of the box. His shot takes a small deflection off Richards, but it's enough to beat Henderson, and the ball finds the far corner. Wow! What a game the Frenchman is having. Nonchalant brilliance.
GOAL! Crystal Palace 1-2 Manchester City (Donnarumma OG 57)
Direct from the free-kick, Palace have their first goal of the Premier League season! Pino takes the free-kick he won, and curls a delicious shot towards the top corner from 30 yards ... the ball clatters against the crossbar, rebounds off the diving Donnarumma and rebounds into the net! Game on!
GOAL! Crystal Palace 0-2 Manchester City (Cherki 54)
An impish, delightful finish! How on earth has Cherki scored that. Palace gave the ball away carelessly in midfield and City pounced, Foden picking up the ball. He fed Cherki, who kept his balance, somehow darting around three Palace defenders and poked his finish past Henderson. The ball rolled slowly, tantalisingly, into the net, as if Cherki was deliberately taking the micky.
53 min: Semenyo has been City's biggest threat in open play, but Khalaili has done a good job in neutralising the City winger. There hasn't been much attacking thrust from Palace's new man, but he's had his hands full.
51 min: Nketiah, playing off the left tonight, drives forward, plays a one-two with the underlapping Mitchell, but can't find a finish. Mitchell fizzes a pass/cross across goal and it came at Nketiah too quickly. The forward couldn't sort his feet out and his finish was well wide.
49 min: Corner for City. In the middle Haaland and Strand Larsen are wrestling each other for space, speaking (presumably) Norwegian to each other. Both are smiling, ear to ear. A deep corner is delivered to O'Reilly at the back post, but Cherki can't make anything of it.
47 min: No changes from either side. Foden continues to look uncomfortable on that right flank. He is not a winger, we know this, and it's not a surprise to see City linked with Everton's Iliman Ndiaye after the departure of Savinho. City have also agreed a €37.5m (£34m) deal for the Palmeiras winger Allan Elias on Monday, and are monitoring Liverpool's Cody Gakpo.
"I narrowly avoided being knocked down by three cars in 90 seconds on my motorbike today," emails Paul Moody. "I live in Brazil so I'm just wondering have I used all my luck or can Palace win this game 2-1?"
Got a minute to spare? Why not try our daily Premier League trivia game, On the ball? Every day a star player past or present is hidden behind nine clues. How many will you need to identify them? It's available in the Guardian apps.
43 min: Foden is back on the right wing and beats Mitchell with a bit of trickery, but Haaland can't get his header right in the middle. Wharton is back on, so Palace are back to full strength.
41 min: Good battling by Wharton, who takes a whack for his troubles. The former Blackburn man gets gingerly to his feet, but he's OK. Serves him right for having such tiny shin pads. In the stands, sitting just above Palace chairman Steve Parish, a pensive Thomas Tuchel looks on. Wharton will have to go off for a minute as part of the new rules: when play is stopped for an injury, players will be required to leave for at least one minute (an increase from the 30 seconds previously used by the Premier League).
